paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this passage is shouting at us: the house of the LORD gets prepared with care. Solomon builds on Mount Moriah, the place where the LORD had appeared to his father David (2 Chronicles 3:1). Then the details keep coming, gold on the beams, gold on the doors, even gold nails (2 Chronicles 3:7, 9). I once eyeballed a batch and ended up with a cookie shaped like a puddle, so I respect a builder who doesn't skip the small stuff.

Notice how many hands it takes, too. Solomon makes the furnishings, and Huram finishes a long list of bronze work for the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 4:11, 16). There is so much bronze that the weight of it could not be determined (2 Chronicles 4:18). I think that tells us preparing is rarely one big moment. It's a lot of steady work, piece after piece, until the job is done.

That matters for you, baker, because getting ready works the same way. Solomon prepared the house of the LORD piece by piece, and I fill cookie boxes for the Marriage Supper of the Lamb the same way, one at a time. Revelation 19:7 says, "His bride has made herself ready," so I'm glad to have you at my side. Every time you open the Word, you add one more small piece, so keep your apron on, because this story isn't over.
